children: The Finance Ministry says existing employees’ service conditions and pension benefits will be protected under the proposed Rs 52,878 crore stake sale

The government has said legitimate concerns of IDBI Bank employees and other stakeholders have been addressed through provisions in the share purchase agreement for the lender’s proposed privatisation, even as employee associations continue to oppose the transaction.

Minister of State for Finance Pankaj Chaudhary told the Lok Sabha that safeguards for existing employees and other stakeholders had been incorporated into the agreement. The response came amid questions about the potential impact of the proposed sale on employees and whether the government had consulted bank staff and their representatives.

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved the sale of a 60.72 per cent stake in IDBI Bank to 10955230 Canada Inc., a subsidiary of Fairfax Financial Holdings, for Rs 52,878 crore. The transaction involves the government selling its 30.48 per cent holding and Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) divesting its 30.24 per cent stake. Following the sale, the government will retain 15 per cent and LIC 19 per cent.

The Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) has separately stated that existing employees’ service conditions will remain protected and pension benefits will be safeguarded through a dedicated pension fund.

However, the United Forum of IDBI Officers and Employees has disputed claims that employee representatives were consulted during the process. The forum has called for the transaction to be reviewed, citing concerns over employee safeguards, the bank’s valuation and the implications of transferring control to a foreign investor. It has also sought greater transparency over the valuation methodology and transaction terms.

The proposed disinvestment process began with the publication of a preliminary information memorandum on 7 October 2022, inviting expressions of interest from potential bidders. The transaction remains subject to the required regulatory approvals and completion procedures.
The competing positions highlight the importance of employee protections and consultation as the government advances the strategic sale of the bank.
